chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it, said:

It was said to him (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! Sometimes there is danger for me from the one whom I fear, so it is not possible to place the twig upon what you have narrated to us.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Enter it (in the grave) wherever it is possible.'

key_terms.الْجَرِيدَةِ: The twig placed in the grave

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one cannot place the grave twig in the standard location due to fear or difficulty?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the principle of *al-rukhas* (concessions) in Shia jurisprudence, demonstrating how ritual obligations adapt to practical constraints like fear or physical limitation. It underscores the scholarly view that the essence of the act—placing the twig—takes precedence over its precise location when circumstances prevent strict adherence to the normative practice.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, raising it, said,

‘It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Sometimes there is danger for me from the one whom I fear, so it is not possible to place the twig upon what you<sup>asws</sup> have narrated to us’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Enter it (in the grave) wherever it is possible’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad in a marfu‘ manner who has said

the following: “It was said to him (the Imam), ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, because of the presence of fear I may not be able to place al-Jaridah (twig of palm tree) as you have told us.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Place them just as it is possible for you to do.’”
